name: Persistent field identity with semantic instruction relationships
summary: A form field remains understandable through an appropriate persistent label, relevant guidance and programmatic associations, including group labels where meaningful.
problem: A control can lose its purpose when transient placeholder text disappears or group context exists only visually.
context: Text inputs, selections and related choice groups where users need to understand a question and constraints throughout entry.
observed_solution: Use descriptive persistent identification, programmatic label/description connections, and legend/group semantics for related controls; present required/format hints as appropriate rather than using placeholder text as the sole identity.
rationale: WCAG 3.3.2 labels/instructions and 1.3.1 info/relations (O01/O07), WAI explicit labels and fieldsets (O12/O13/O14), GOV text labels/fieldset (O18/O23), USWDS text input guidance (O25/O26), Primer documentation and pinned FormControl id/wiring mechanics (O31/O36/O37/O38). Direct evidence concerns obligations/guidance and source mechanics; gains in completion are inferred and not measured.
tradeoffs: Visible labels and hints consume space, especially on narrow screens.
Too many examples/hints may overwhelm simple choices.
Programmatic naming alone may not resolve visible ambiguity.
applicability: Fields whose purpose or constraints might otherwise be ambiguous during entry.
Related choices requiring a common question context.
non_applicability: A purely decorative mark with no data-entry control.
A standalone control already clearly named through another legitimate accessible technique may not need the same visible layout.
accessibility_implications: Check associated accessible names, descriptions, required state and choice-group naming; no screen-reader tests executed.
performance_implications: No meaningful performance measurement; additional helper elements increase markup but effect unknown.
responsive_implications: Do not separate labels/hints from their controls when stacking, per accepted W03/W04 guidance.
implementation_notes: Not a universal component library, label position, asterisk/optional convention or fieldset-for-every-input rule.
Do not use placeholder as the only accessible identification.
Accessible name and visible label may differ in justified contexts.

counterexamples.summary: A compact search control can be identified by a valid alternative accessible name where context is clear, though placeholder-only purpose remains risky.
counterexamples.context: Recognizable, separately accessible search field with explicit ARIA label.

version_context: WCAG 2.2 Recommendation 2024; official live WAI/GOV/USWDS/Primer docs; pinned primer/react@7f5303d803986887187d86dcebaeda22a4dc6823
